description: Questions for the cs_book KB (English sources). The 'cs' set is the cross-lingual one: Czech questions against English sources.
authoring: Hand-written by the implementing agent against the committed KB texts (no LLM endpoint was reachable); regenerate or extend with `scripts/bench_retrieval.py generate-questions`.
relevance: A retrieved item is relevant when its excerpt contains the answer span (case-, accent-, whitespace- and hyphenation-insensitive).

en.question: Which branch of AI produces new content such as text, code or images?
en.answer: Generative AI is the branch that produces new content

en.question: What is the instruction given to a generative model called?
en.answer: The instruction a user gives to a generative model is called a prompt

en.question: What is the core training task of a large language model?
en.answer: given a sequence of text, predict the next piece of text

en.question: Roughly how much of an English word does one token correspond to?
en.answer: one token corresponds to roughly three quarters of an English word

en.question: Why do languages like Czech need more tokens for the same text?
en.answer: languages with rich inflection such as Czech need more tokens for the same content

en.question: What is the vector of numbers assigned to each token called?
en.answer: Each token is mapped to a vector of numbers called an embedding

en.question: Which technique lets a model answer using passages retrieved from trusted documents?
en.answer: This technique is the basis of retrieval-augmented generation

en.question: Why does a language model know nothing about recent events?
en.answer: every model has a knowledge cut-off date

en.question: What do enterprise licences usually guarantee about conversations?
en.answer: Institutional or enterprise licences usually guarantee that conversations are not used to train future models

en.question: What is a hallucination in generative AI?
en.answer: A hallucination is a fluent, confident statement that is false

en.question: What kind of references can language models invent?
en.answer: Models may invent references to articles that do not exist

en.question: How can bias appear subtly in generated exercises?
en.answer: for example in the default names chosen for characters in an exercise

en.question: What happens if you ask a model about the current exam schedule of a course?
en.answer: Asking a model about the current exam schedule of a course will produce an invented answer

en.question: Can language models take ethical decisions on behalf of a teacher?
en.answer: They cannot take ethical decisions on behalf of a teacher

en.question: What is the most common mistake when writing a prompt?
en.answer: Omitting the audience is the most common mistake

en.question: What is few-shot prompting?
en.answer: In few-shot prompting the instruction is followed by a small number of worked examples

en.question: Which prompting technique asks the model to reason step by step?
en.answer: Chain-of-thought prompting asks the model to reason step by step

en.question: Does assigning a role give the model new expertise?
en.answer: but it does not give the model any expertise it did not already have

en.question: Where do teachers report the largest time savings from generative tools?
en.answer: Teachers report the largest time savings when they use generative tools for first drafts

en.question: What should you ask for besides the correct answer when generating quiz questions?
en.answer: the typical misconception behind each wrong option

en.question: How should a teacher calibrate a rubric drafted with AI?
en.answer: calibrate it on a few real student submissions

en.question: What should students be told about automated feedback?
en.answer: students should be told clearly which parts of the feedback process are automated

en.question: How can generative tools improve accessibility for students?
en.answer: producing plain-language summaries or transcripts

en.question: How can teachers build AI literacy in class?
en.answer: Teachers can build this literacy by demonstrating a hallucination in class

en.question: What five principles should the use of generative AI in teaching rest on?
en.answer: transparency, privacy, fairness, integrity and accountability

en.question: What does the principle of fairness require?
en.answer: Fairness requires that no student is disadvantaged because they cannot afford a paid tool

en.question: Who is accountable for a grade when a teacher uses a model to grade short answers?
en.answer: remains accountable for the grade and must be able to explain it

en.question: Which student data can count as personal data under the GDPR?
en.answer: Student names, identification numbers, grades, submitted work and even writing style can be personal data

en.question: What agreement must the university have with an external AI provider?
en.answer: a data processing agreement with the provider

en.question: What does data minimisation mean?
en.answer: only the data that are strictly necessary for the task should be processed

en.question: What should be carried out before deploying a tool that processes student data at scale?
en.answer: a data protection impact assessment (DPIA) should be carried out before deployment

en.question: When was the EU AI Act adopted?
en.answer: known as the AI Act, was adopted in 2024

en.question: Is education a high-risk area under the AI Act?
en.answer: Education is explicitly named among the high-risk areas

en.question: When does a chat assistant become a high-risk AI system?
en.answer: the same technology becomes high-risk when it is used to assign grades automatically

en.question: What is a typical example of an assignment where using an AI tool is required?
en.answer: Critique of an AI-generated text

en.question: What should a declaration of AI use contain?
en.answer: the declaration should name the tool, describe what it was used for, and include the key prompts

en.question: In APA style, who is named as the author when citing a generative AI model?
en.answer: names the company that developed the model as the author

en.question: Which texts do AI detectors frequently flag incorrectly?
en.answer: detectors frequently flag texts written by non-native speakers as generated

en.question: Is an AI detector score evidence of misconduct?
en.answer: A detector score is therefore not evidence of misconduct

en.question: What are process portfolios?
en.answer: Process portfolios, in which students submit drafts, notes and reflections

en.question: Where should a course redesign start?
en.answer: A course redesign should start from the learning outcomes
